articles.title: Google Ads clicks but no leads? Check the buying journey.
articles.summary: A practical guide to search intent, landing pages and conversion tracking when Google Ads brings visitors but few useful enquiries.

sections.title: A click is not proof of buying intent
sections.body: Not every Google Ads click comes from someone ready to buy. Open the search terms report and look for research queries, job searches or locations you do not cover. A campaign can have an impressive click-through rate while sending the wrong visitors to your site. Start by checking whether the searches match what your business actually sells.

sections.title: Check what people see after clicking your ad
sections.body: Imagine clicking an ad for a particular service and arriving on a homepage that asks you to explore everything. That extra work often loses people. The landing page should confirm the service, who it is for, where it is offered and how to ask a question or request a quote.

sections.title: Test the enquiry before judging the campaign
sections.body: Before you turn up your Google Ads budget, send a test enquiry from your phone and a desktop browser. Did the form submit? Did the sales team receive it? Was the conversion counted once, rather than when someone simply clicked the button? Missing enquiries can be a website or tracking problem, not an advertising problem.

sections.title: Choose the fix that matches the problem
sections.body: Fix the problem you have evidence for. Tighten search targeting if intent is wrong; clarify the landing page if visitors are confused; repair event tracking if submissions are not counted properly. Make one meaningful change at a time, then check whether more enquiries are from people you can actually help.

articles.title: Website traffic but no enquiries? Find the missing next step.
articles.summary: Review your offer, mobile experience and form journey before investing in more traffic. Connect each finding to a practical website improvement.

sections.title: Check who visits before changing the design
sections.body: A visit from someone looking for general advice is different from a visit from someone comparing service providers. Review which pages attract visitors and the searches or links that bring them in. You may find that traffic has grown around a topic that does not naturally lead to your services.

sections.title: Answer the questions before the form
sections.body: People rarely enquire when they cannot tell whether a service is right for them. Explain who you work with, what is included, what happens after an enquiry and any limitations you can share. A real example or clearly described process can help more than another brightly coloured button.

sections.title: Make it easier to contact you
sections.body: Try contacting your own business on a phone. Look for confusing navigation, forms that reject valid inputs, contact details that are hard to find and questions that appear too early. Collect only what you need to respond properly, and tell visitors what they can expect next.

sections.title: Make changes you can evaluate
sections.body: Choose a few changes linked to the problem you found. If traffic is modest, a formal A/B test may never reach a useful sample size. In that case, use customer feedback, usability checks and sensible before-and-after monitoring—without claiming proof you do not have.

source.label: Google Analytics: Events and key events

articles.title: How to measure lead quality before increasing your budget.
articles.summary: Use clear qualification criteria, enquiry sources and sales feedback to understand which marketing brings suitable prospects.

sections.title: Decide what makes an enquiry suitable
sections.body: A lead is useful only when it matches the work your team can deliver. Agree a simple definition with sales: service need, location, budget or business fit, and whether the person is ready for a conversation. A travel enquiry and a B2B software demo will need different criteria.

sections.title: Count enquiries and check whether they are useful
sections.body: Keep a record of how many enquiries arrive, how many your team accepts and how many turn into serious opportunities. Look at the source where tracking allows. Ten well-matched leads may be worth more than a hundred forms from people outside your service area.

sections.title: Feed the learning back into acquisition
sections.body: Ask sales why leads are rejected. If a Google Ads campaign attracts the wrong location or company size, that feedback can guide targeting and landing-page copy. Offline conversion imports may help when they are configured correctly and the relevant privacy and consent requirements are met.

sections.title: Respect measurement limits
sections.body: No dashboard sees every interaction before someone buys. CRM gaps, duplicate leads and long sales cycles can distort channel comparisons. Make those limits clear in your reporting and evaluate campaigns over a window that reflects your actual buying process.

source.label: Google Ads: About offline conversion imports

articles.title: International SEO: build pages for customers, not just countries.
articles.summary: Plan useful market content, genuine service coverage and clear buying information for international customers.

sections.title: Start with the market you can actually serve
sections.body: Before building a page for another country, check what your business can actually deliver there. Visitors need to know about remote support, working hours, languages and relevant commercial terms. Do not imply that you have an office or local team where you do not.

sections.title: Create a regional page when the offer changes
sections.body: A useful market page should have a reason to exist beyond the country name in its title. Perhaps the service areas, language, regulatory information or customer questions differ. Explain those real differences; otherwise a strong international service page may be more helpful.

sections.title: Keep the technical signals aligned
sections.body: Give each genuine regional page its own accurate title, canonical and internal links. Where you offer real language or regional equivalents, hreflang can help describe the relationship. It cannot make identical translated-looking pages useful to local customers by itself.

sections.title: Measure the enquiries that fit
sections.body: Judge a market by whether the enquiries fit the service you can provide, not by impressions alone. Review questions from prospective customers and update the page to answer them. Expand into another country only when your delivery and content genuinely justify it.

source.label: Google Search: Managing multilingual and multiregional sites
